subject: Re: MAP — unit economics pinch points, assumptions & close timeline
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medispec.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions we need for procurement

Aditya / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the flow and the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to get a consolidated set of assumptions for our MAP so we can align finance and legal on the road to POC signoff. Specifically they want: tokens-per-dollar sensitivity, expected on‑peak/off‑peak traffic shapes, and any caching/batching preconditions that materially change unit cost.

Can you send a short doc/table showing: 1) tokens/$ at baseline and two sensitivity points, 2) what caching or prefix reuse we require to hit the best-case numbers, and 3) how latency SLOs change if we switch to 8k vs 32k context or add aggressive batching? Procurement wants to confirm these items before we finalize the timeline (they're pushing for a July POC start).

Also, is there anything in your MAP that would force a longer procurement cycle (SOC2 evidence items, private deployment add-ons, or long lead-time hardware)?

Thanks — I can loop in legal if you prefer a single thread.

Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of Platform Integrations — Medispec

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medispec.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions we need for procurement

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a spreadsheet (medispec_map_v2.xlsx) with a compact cost model and a CSV with the token profiles I used. High-level summary below so procurement has something readable up front.

Key numbers (baseline = 8k context, conservative traffic, no heavy prefetch):
- Baseline tokens/$: 200k tokens per $1 at conservative batch sizing (latency SLO 150–250ms tail).
- Mid-case (moderate batching & prefix cache): 320k tokens per $.
- Best-case (aggressive batching + prefix reuse, 75% cache hit on common instructions): 600k tokens per $.

What moves these levers:
- Caching: prefix/KV cache is most impactful for repeated system prompts or few-shot templates. If you can standardize prompts or host instruction templates, expect 2–3x improvement in tokens/$ for conversational flows.
- Batching: throughput efficiency improves when requests are queueable and can tolerate slight added latency (we show gains if you can accept 30–50ms additional median latency).
- Context length: moving from 8k to 32k increases per-request compute ~2.4x in our benchmarks (depends on model architecture). If you require 32k for retrieval-heavy workflows, plan for approximately 40–60% unit-cost uplift versus 8k baseline unless you also increase batching and cache hit rates.

Procurement / timeline impacts:
- SOC2/infosec pack: we can provide our SOC2 summary and an audit artifact bundle in 3 business days once NDA is signed. Full private deployment + HSM integration adds ~4–6 weeks to delivery.
- Dedicated hardware (if you want reserved GPUs): lead time depends on region and configuration; typical procurement + setup for Dedicated is 3–5 weeks after contract signature.

I included a few scenario tabs in the spreadsheet: steady-state P50/P95 cost, a 3-month POC burn estimate given your projected 1.2M daily tokens, and a sensitivity sweep for cache hit rate (0–80%).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the traffic profile (attached sample_token_profile.csv is my assumed distribution).
2) We lock MAP milestones (POC start, acceptance criteria, ramp dates) — I can propose a timeline if July POC start is required.
3) I’ll drop SOC2 artifacts to your legal/procurement folder if you share the contact.

If helpful I can also run a short A/B: same workload with/without prefix caching to demonstrate delta for your engineers.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medispec.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions we need for procurement

Looping in a couple of operational guardrails so procurement has clarity on acceptance and risk. Short bullets below — please include these in the MAP draft.

Acceptance & gating notes:
- Unit-econ acceptance criteria: POC must demonstrate <= X tokens per $ (choose the mid-case target) for at least two representative flows over a 72-hour window with production-like concurrency. Put the exact thresholds in the MAP milestone.
- Regression monitoring: add a smoke eval set (10 prompts) to the MAP that we run daily during POC; any quality regression or >10% delta in tokens/$ triggers rollback or scope change.
- Batching/latency tradeoff: call out the allowed latency budget per route. For routes with strict UI latency (<200ms), batching gains will be limited; mark those as "non-batchable." For async or background routes we can enable maximum batch windows (up to 50ms queueing).
- Caching design doc: require a short appendix describing prefix-key strategy — teams should commit to at least one canonical system prompt and a canonical few-shot template to unlock cache benefits.

Operational risks to surface to Medispec:
- If they require 32k context for all flows, expect extended tuning and a corresponding cost uplift that may push them out of the July POC unless they accept narrower acceptance criteria.
- Private deployment or additional compliance add-ons increase procurement time; recommend they scope these in parallel to the POC rather than as POC blockers.

Aditya / Monica: can we put the acceptance thresholds into the MAP draft and produce a one‑page scoring rubric? Tom, if mid-case targets look reasonable I’ll approve the proposed July timeline from our side.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medispec.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions we need for procurement

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A few clarifications from our side that will help finalize the MAP and keep us on the July POC ramp: 

1) Traffic profile: average 1.2M tokens/day, spikes up to 3.5M tokens/day during peak experiments, ~70% conversational reuse expected (many standardized instruction templates). See attached sample_token_profile.csv — we can provide finer logs if needed.
2) Context: primary UI flows use 8k, retrieval-assisted reports may use 32k but only for batch jobs (not interactive dashboards). If you model 32k only for background jobs, that should reduce the overall uplift.
3) SOC2: legal confirmed they only need SOC2 type II summary and a short control matrix; we can handle that in parallel and won't block POC start.

We are comfortable with the mid-case tokens/$ as the MAP target for acceptance as long as we have the smoke eval and the scoring rubric. Please send the revised MAP with thresholds and the one-page rubric and we’ll route that in procurement this afternoon.

Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of Platform Integrations — Medispec
